newsitem.title: POLAND: Flotation of first Polish power firm seen in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Flotation of first Polish power firm seen in 1998.

text.p: The issue prospectus of EC Bedzin SA heating and power company, earmarked to blaze a trail as the first Polish energy firm to be floated, should be ready by the end of this year, Bedzin chief said on Wednesday.

"The advising consortium led by Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) assumes that the issue prospectus for Elektrocieplownia Bedzin should be ready by the end of 1997," president Jacek Uminski told a news conference.

Uminski said the flotation of the treasury-owned company, whose full name is Elektrocieplownia Bedzin SA, would be carried out through a new share issue and be treated as a pilot project for further privatisations in the sector.
"After an analysis and a search for investors it will be possible to determine what is the interest of the domestic and foreign capital in this sector of the industry," he said.

Uminski said the firm, based in the southern town of Bedzin, wanted to attract several institutional investors as well as other heating firms as investors and would seek listing on Warsaw bourse's main market in 1998.

Uminski said Bedzin together with Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) acting as the treasury ministry advisor would by mid-year prepare a plan which would detail to whom and in what proportions the new shares would be offered.

In a statement distributed at the conference Bedzin said the general plan assumed that new shares would be offered to domestic and foreign retail and institutional investors, four neighbouring municipalities, employees and management.

It said the flotation should attract a group of institutional investors from among domestic and foreign financial institutions, international power companies, large energy recipients, fuels and equipment suppliers.
Uminski said it would be up to the treasury ministry to decide how many Bedzin shares would remain in the state's hands and how big stakes could be offered to various groups of investors.
Jaroslaw Biernacki, BGZ deputy head, also present, said that within a few weeks the advising consortium would discuss with the treasury ministry a broad outline of the Bedzin privatisation plan.
Uminski said the proceeds from the issue would be used for investments in machinery and equity investments aimed at creating a regional holding group.
He said Bedzin, employing 400, had an estimated net profit of 4-4.5 million zlotys on sales of 70 million zlotys in 1996.
Uminski said he would not give a 1997 earnings forecasts because it was not clear yet what the prices of coal would be this year.
